title: Introduce KMS Federation Operator + SealedSecret Guardian for cross-cluster HSM key propagation
author: Lena Ortega
description: Context: customers deploying Redwood Private across multiple air-gapped datacenters requested automated, auditable propagation of HSM-wrapped keys and TLS certs between primary KMS instances and read-only local KMS proxies. This PR introduces a KMS Federation Operator (KFO) plus a SealedSecret Guardian daemonset to orchestrate safe key material replication, reconciled by Terraform/Helm hooks. Motivation: avoid manual sealed secret unseal workflows during cluster join, reduce time-to-recovery for HSM failovers, and provide an auditable policy-based propagation model. Scope: operator CRDs + controller, Helm chart changes (upgrade hooks, post-install job), Terraform module for federation resources, upgrade/rollback safe hooks, docs and test harness. Checklist: [x] CRD and controller implementation; [x] Helm templates and upgrade-hook jobs; [x] Terraform module to provision federation roles and KMS ACLs; [x] Migration job (idempotent) to materialize existing sealed secrets into guardian-managed stores; [x] E2E smoke test in perf-canary; [x] Docs/upgrade guide and rollback notes. Design notes: - KFO implements a controller that watches KMSFederation CR and ensures lockless, nonce-based propagation of HSM-wrapped KEKs to target clusters via sealed secrets. - SealedSecret Guardian runs with minimal privileges; it consumes Vault/Unseal operators only for bootstrap and stores encrypted blobs in sealedsecret CRs. - Propagation policy allows white/blacklists of key IDs and optional TTL-based refreshing. - Operator uses a confirmation handshake (signed nonce) to prevent replay attacks; unit tests cover nonce lifecycle and on-disk rotated key caches. Backwards compatibility: migration job will no-op if cluster already managed by existing rotation tooling. Rollback strategy: helm pre-delete hook removes Guardian with a drain window; federation CRs are annotated with previous-state snapshots to allow safe rollback. Security review: keys never reside unwrapped on disk; all operations require KMS delegated roles one-time tokens. See SUP-4517 for customer repro.
